system_description.narrative_title: War, Energy and Elections: An Open Order Under Strain
system_description.narrative_summary: The international system is being driven by interacting crisis streams: active wars (notably Iran-related Gulf tensions and the Russia–Ukraine war) that are reshaping energy flows and corporate profits; simultaneous political turbulence from major elections and legal battles that are reconfiguring domestic-to-foreign policy linkages; and deepening great-power competition and strategic realignments across Europe and the Indo‑Pacific. These processes form a highly connected, open system with strong feedbacks between battlefield dynamics, commodity markets, central‑bank and bond markets, supply chains and electoral politics, producing elevated volatility and policy uncertainty.
system_description.scope: States, alliances and blocs; major non-state military actors; international institutions (UN, G20, EU, IMF/World Bank); global markets (energy, commodities, finance); strategic supply chains and logistics nodes (shipping, ports, data centers); leading tech and defence firms; and domestic electoral/legal processes in systemically important countries.
system_description.super_system: The globalized political‑economic system (the interconnected human socio‑economic and security order embedded in the Anthropocene-era global economy).

variables.name: Russia-Ukraine war
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine, backed respectively by varying international partners, remain locked in a protracted war whose shifting frontlines, missile and drone campaigns and Black Sea disruptions are reshaping European security and logistics.

variables.name: U.S.–Iran / Gulf confrontation
variables.description: The United States, Iran, Gulf states and regional proxies are engaged in a high-risk confrontation marked by tanker attacks, naval incidents and intensive mediation efforts that raise the threat of wider US‑Iran hostilities.

variables.name: China‑West strategic competition
variables.description: China and the United States, together with European and Asian partners, are deepening a systemic rivalry combining technology and trade decoupling, export controls and growing military/maritime assertiveness that is remaking supply chains and alliance choices.

variables.name: Global energy market shock
variables.description: Oil and refining markets worldwide are being reconfigured by supply shocks from regional wars and OPEC+ output decisions, producing sharp price volatility, record refining margins and a reorientation of storage, investment and fuel-security strategies.

variables.name: Monetary policy and market volatility
variables.description: Major central banks (Fed, ECB, BOJ) and global capital markets are in flux as shifting inflation dynamics, rate decisions and leadership changes drive bond-market volatility and contest the next phase of global interest‑rate policy.
